chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Amriki, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Matar, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man who wants to buy a house, or land, or a servant, and to give him a wage (for the purchase). He said, 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.جُعْل: A fixed wage or commission paid for a specific service or transaction, distinct from salary.
key_terms.خَادِماً: A servant or slave, referring to domestic service in the context of the narration.
key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm in it; a common juristic phrase indicating permissibility (jawaaz).

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay a commission or wage for facilitating the purchase of a house, land, or servant in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* validates the practice of *ju'l* (commission), affirming the permissibility of compensating an agent or broker for facilitating the acquisition of real estate, land, or servants. It establishes a foundational legal precedent in Shia jurisprudence for commercial agency (*wakalah*) and brokerage fees, distinguishing them from prohibited usury or uncertainty (*gharar*).
